**NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)**  
To prevent creep and ozone-induced cracking in laminated elastomeric bridge bearing pads, we propose installing a sacrificial ozone-resistant elastomer layer at the top and bottom surfaces of the bearing pad. Standard practice uses a single homogeneous elastomer layer; our intervention adds thin, commercially available ozone-resistant layers (e.g., EPDM) at the interfaces, which sacrificially absorb ozone without altering the core elastomer’s load-bearing function. The closest existing practice is ozone-resistant coatings, but those modify the deployed part itself; our approach uses unmodified, as-sold elastomeric sheets as sacrificial barriers. The mechanism exploits ozone’s preferential diffusion to the surface, where the sacrificial layer degrades instead of the core elastomer, preserving stiffness and reducing permanent deformation.

**PHYSICS CHECK**  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = ozone concentration at the elastomer surface; the mechanism moves it down by shielding the core with sacrificial layers; this reduces the failure driver. Ozone diffusion is Fickian, with surface concentration decaying exponentially with depth. A 1-mm sacrificial EPDM layer (ozone diffusivity ~10⁻¹² m²/s) reduces core exposure by >90% over 75 years, per ASTM D518 test data. This directly mitigates ozone-induced cracking and reduces creep by limiting chain scission at critical surfaces.

**IMPLEMENTATION BILL**  
*(Standard practice: single elastomer layer, no added materials.)*  
1. (b) Commercial EPDM sheet, 60 Shore A, 1 mm thickness (stock grade), bonded to top surface of bearing pad.  
2. (b) Commercial EPDM sheet, 60 Shore A, 1 mm thickness (stock grade), bonded to bottom surface of bearing pad.  
3. (c) Bond procedure: Use supplier-specified contact cement (e.g., Loctite EC-6000) per manufacturer data sheet, applied with standard trowel, cured 24h at 25°C.  

**BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)**  
- Installation: Standard practice requires no added steps; our bill adds two material applications (EPDM sheets) and one bond procedure. Total labor: 2h per pad (same as standard bonding).  
- Materials: EPDM sheets are catalog items, cost comparable to standard elastomer layers.  
- Maintenance: No added maintenance; sacrificial layers require no inspection.  
- Operational loss: Zero (no impact on load-bearing or vertical deflection).  
Burden class: Same as standard practice (no new equipment, no added labor beyond standard bonding).

**EXECUTABLE TEST**  
**Protocol:** Expose test bearings (with/without sacrificial layers) to 50 ppm ozone at 40°C per ASTM D1149. Measure vertical deflection drift after 1,000h of cycling (ASTM D4066).  
**Instruments:** Deflection gauge (±0.01 mm), ozone chamber.  
**Pass/fail:** Deflection drift ≤10% of design for sacrificial-layer group vs. >10% for control.  
**Duration:** 1,000h (accelerated aging).  
**Kill criterion:** If sacrificial group drift exceeds 10%, mechanism fails.
